newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Lasmo gains after Pakistan gas find.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Lasmo gains after Pakistan gas find.

text.p: Shares in Lasmo Plc, Britain's second biggest hydrocarbon production and exploration firm, powered 4.7 percent ahead on Tuesday after the company reported a major gas find in Pakistan.

The discovery in the southern province of Sindh has estimated reserves of two trillion cubic feet (tcf) of gas. This would translate in a share for Lasmo of 130 million barrels of oil equivalent or twice its production in 1996, Lasmo said.
"This is in potential a significant discovery," a Lasmo spokesman said.

Lasmo shares gained 11 pence ($0.18) a share to 234 in mid-afternoon trade and broker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett upgraded the stocks to "hold" from "sell" following the discovery in the Kirthar concession.

Lasmo still has to do seismic research and more drilling before actually booking any reserves. Some might already be booked by the end of this year, but it will take a little longer before Lasmo gets a real clear picture of the field, the company said.
"The two trillion may turn out to be one or it may turn out to be significantly more. By next year we should have a much clearer view," the spokesman said.
A decision whether to develop the field may be taken in 1999, while the first production might come onstream in 2001 if all goes smoothly, he said.

Lasmo and Shell Exploration Pakistan BV both have a 47.5 percent working interest in Kirthar. Pakistan's state-owned Oil and Gas Development Corporation has 5.0 percent, but has the right to back in for 20 percent.
Lasmo's announcement follows a more cautious statement by the Pakistani government, which on Monday said estimated reserves were more than one tcf.
Lasmo, which made the find and evaluated the results, said the difference stemmed from a more conservative risk assessment by Pakistan.
"There is a lot of uncertainty, but the mid-point in our view is two tcf. We think the Pakistan government is very conservative," the Lasmo spokesman said. ($1=.6161 Pound)
